Rashi on Shabbat 88b:1:1.hebrew: דסגינן בשלימותא - התהלכנו עמו בתום לב, כדרך העושים מאהבה, וסמכנו עליו שאל יטעננו בדבר שלא נוכל לעמוד:
Rashi on Shabbat 88b:1:1.english: Who proceed wholeheartedly - We walked with Him in integrity of heart, in the manner of those who act out of love, and we relied upon Him that He would not burden us with something that we would not be able to withstand.

Rashi on Shabbat 88b:2:1.english: You have ravished my heart - You have drawn me near.

Rashi on Shabbat 88b:2:2.hebrew: בתחלה - בקבלה שקבלתם, אחת הוא אצלם, ולבסוף כשקיימתם, שתים יש:
Rashi on Shabbat 88b:2:2.english: At first - In the acceptance that you accepted [the Torah], there is one [eye] with them; and in the end, when you fulfill [it], there are two.

Rashi on Shabbat 88b:2:3.hebrew: עלובה - חצופה, דעולבנא לישנא דחוצפא היא, והכי אמר במס' גיטין:
Rashi on Shabbat 88b:2:3.english: Insolent - Audacious, for ulbana is an expression of audacity, and so it says in Tractate Gittin.

Rashi on Shabbat 88b:2:4.english: Is promiscuous under her wedding canopy - Like Israel when they stood at Sinai and made the [Golden] Calf.

Rashi on Shabbat 88b:2:5.english: At his table - In his wedding canopy.

Rashi on Shabbat 88b:2:6.hebrew: ועדיין חביבותא היא גבן - אע"פ שהמקרא מספר בגנותנו, הראה לנו לשון חבה, מדלא כתיב הסריח:
Rashi on Shabbat 88b:2:6.english: And it is still affection toward us - Although the verse speaks to our disparagement, He showed us an expression of affection, since it is not written, "it reeked."

Rashi on Shabbat 88b:2:7.english: Gave - [It] left its good fragrance to others.

Rashi on Shabbat 88b:2:8.english: Those who are insulted and do not insult - Others come against them with insolence, and they [do] not [come] against others.

Rashi on Shabbat 88b:2:9.english: [They] act out of love of the Omnipresent and are joyful in suffering - over the insult that comes upon them.

Rashi on Shabbat 88b:3:1.english: A great host - All the nations.

Rashi on Shabbat 88b:3:2.english: [Just] as a hammer - the rock is divided through it into several splinters.

Rashi on Shabbat 88b:4:1.hebrew: למיימינים - עסוקים בכל כחם וטרודים לדעת סודה, כאדם המשתמש ביד ימינו, שהיא עיקר:
Rashi on Shabbat 88b:4:1.english: To those who are right-handed - [They are] engaged with all their strength and engrossed in knowing its secret, like a person who uses his right hand, which is primary.

Rashi on Shabbat 88b:4:2.hebrew: קושרים לו שני כתרים - לדבור שהיה בו ממש ונראה, כדכתיב רואים את הקולות (שמות כ׳:ט״ו):
Rashi on Shabbat 88b:4:2.english: Two crowns are tied to it - To the utterance, which had substance and was visible, as it is written: "they saw the sounds" (Exodus 20:15).

Rashi on Shabbat 88b:4:3.hebrew: אע"פ שמיצר ומימר לי דודי - בעגל, שאמר הורד עדיך:
Rashi on Shabbat 88b:4:3.english: Even though my beloved causes me suffering and bitterness - [With the sin of] the [Golden] Calf, when He said, "Remove your ornaments."

Rashi on Shabbat 88b:4:4.hebrew: בין שדי ילין - אמר מיד לעשות לו משכן, להיות מצומצמת שכינתו בין שני הבדים שנראי' במקדש ראשון כשני שדים, דוחקין ובולטין בפרוכת שכנגד הפתח:
Rashi on Shabbat 88b:4:4.english: Lies between my breasts - [He] immediately commanded to make a Tabernacle for Him, so that His Divine Presence would be concentrated between the two poles [of the Ark], which appeared in the First Temple like two breasts, pressing and protruding against the curtain that was opposite the entrance.

Rashi on Shabbat 88b:4:5.hebrew: עין גדי - עון עגל שהוא מין בהמה. לשון אחר: לשון עכו"ם, "העורכים לגד שלחן" (ישעיהו ס״ה:י״א):
Rashi on Shabbat 88b:4:5.english: Ein Gedi - [Refers to] the sin of the calf, which is a type of animal. Another explanation: [it is] an expression of idolatry, [as in:] "who set a table for Gad [a pagan deity]" (Isaiah 65:11).

Rashi on Shabbat 88b:4:6.hebrew: שכרמתי - שאספתי להתאוות אלהות הרבה, כדכתיב: ״אלה אלהיך ישראל״ (שמות ל״ב:ד׳):
Rashi on Shabbat 88b:4:6.english: That I collected - That I gathered [for myself] to desire many deities, as it is written: “These are your gods, O Israel” (Exodus 32:4).

Rashi on Shabbat 88b:4:7.hebrew: שכורמים עליו - שמאספין עליו את הבגדים, והוא דף ארוכה ומנוקבת נקבים הרבה, ומניח המוגמר תחתיה, והכלים מתגמרין מדרך הנקבים. לישנא דמיכנש גרסינן:
Rashi on Shabbat 88b:4:7.english: Upon which they gather - [This means] that they gather the garments upon it, and it is a long board perforated with many holes; one places incense underneath it, and the garments are perfumed through the holes. We read [the text as]: "an expression of gathering."

Rashi on Shabbat 88b:5:1.english: [He] made the first [fragrance] pass - To the Garden of Eden.

Rashi on Shabbat 88b:5:2.english: Flowing myrrh - Because He caused them to pass.

Rashi on Shabbat 88b:6:1.english: A bountiful rain - It is written regarding the giving of the Torah in the Book of Psalms.

Rashi on Shabbat 88b:6:2.hebrew: י"ב מיל - זו היא מדת מחניהם, והיו הקרובים לדיבור חוזרין מפחד הקול עד קצה המחנה:
Rashi on Shabbat 88b:6:2.english: Twelve mil - This is the measure of their camp, and those who were close to the utterance would retreat out of fear of the voice to the edge of the camp.

Rashi on Shabbat 88b:6:3.hebrew: מדדין אותן - מסייעין אותן להתקרב מעט מעט, שהיו חלשים, כאשה המדדה את בנה בתחלת הילוכו:
Rashi on Shabbat 88b:6:3.english: Walked them - [They] assisted them to come close little by little, for they were weak, like a woman who walks her son at the beginning of his walking.

Rashi on Shabbat 88b:7:1.hebrew: תתקע"ד דורות - באלפים שנה שקדמה תורה לעולם, היו עתידין דורות הללו להבראות, שנאמר (תהילים ק״ה:ח׳) ״דבר צוה לאלף דור״. וראה הקב"ה שאין העולם מתקיים בלא תורה כל כך, והעבירן ולא בראן, ונתנה לכ"ו דורות, הרי שחסרו תתקע"ד מאלף:
Rashi on Shabbat 88b:7:1.english: 974 generations - During the two thousand years that the Torah preceded the world, these generations were destined to be created, as it is stated (Psalms 105:8), "The word which He commanded to a thousand generations." And the Holy One, Blessed be He, saw that the world could not endure without the Torah for so long, so He passed them over and did not create them, and He gave it to twenty-six generations; thus, 974 were lacking from a thousand.

Rashi on Shabbat 88b:7:2.hebrew: מה אדיר שמך - אדיר הוא הרבה בארץ, ואין ראוי לך ליתן הודך שם כי אם על השמים:
Rashi on Shabbat 88b:7:2.english: How glorious is Your name - It is very glorious on earth, and it is not fitting for You to give Your majesty there, but rather upon the heavens.

Rashi on Shabbat 88b:8:1.english: Shaddai spread from the radiance - [This is] a notarikon [acronym] of [the word] parshez.

Tosafot on Shabbat 88b:2:1.hebrew: ולא כתיב הסריח - לשון מגונה לא היה לו לכתוב; אלא כלומר: ולא כתב "ערב ריחו", דהוה משמע הסריח, אלא כתב "נתן" — לשון חביבות:
Tosafot on Shabbat 88b:2:1.english: And it is not written, "it reeked" - [Scripture] would not write an offensive expression; rather, [Rav] means to say: and it did not write "its fragrance spoiled," which would imply that it reeked, rather it wrote "gave [off]," an expression of affection.

Tosafot on Shabbat 88b:3:1.hebrew: מה פטיש זה מתחלק לכמה ניצוצות - הקשה רבינו שמואל: והא קרא משמע דהפטיש מפוצץ את הסלע, מדלא כתיב "והפטיש יפוצצנו סלע", וכן אנו רואין שהפטיש מפוצץ סלעים; וליכא למיגרס "מה סלע מתחלק לכמה ניצוצות", דהא דיבור — דהיינו תורה — נמשלה לפטיש ולא לסלע. ובקונטרס פי': מה פטיש — מתחלק הסלע על ידו; ואינו מיושב, שהדיבור הוא עצמו מתחלק, ואינו דמיון גמור. ואומר ר"ת דקרא מיירי באבן המפוצץ ברזל, דאמר במדרש חזית: מעשה באחד שקנה סנפירין ובא לבודקה, נתנה על הסדן והכה עליה בקורנס — נחלק הפטיש ונשבר הסדן, וסנפירין לא זז ממקומו, הה"ד: "וכפטיש יפוצץ סלע". ואף על גב דלא כתיב "יפוצצנו סלע", הרבה פסוקים יש כענין זה: "אבנים שחקו מים" (איוב י״ד:י״ט) — פי': שחקו אותן מים. ואתו שפיר דאמר בפ"ק דקדושין (דף ל:): תנא דבי רבי ישמעאל: "בני, אם פגע בך מנוול זה — משכהו לביהמ"ד; ואם אבן הוא — נמוח, שנא': אבנים שחקו מים" — פירוש: שחקו אותם מים; "ואם ברזל הוא — מתפוצץ" — פירוש: אם יצר הרע מתחזק עליו כברזל, מתפוצץ, שנאמר: "וכפטיש יפוצץ סלע". ואף על פי דהתם מדמה יצה"ר לפטיש וכאן מדמה ד"ת לפטיש, אין לחוש, דמקרא אחד יוצא לכמה טעמים:
Tosafot on Shabbat 88b:3:1.english: "Just as this hammer divides into several fragments" - Rabbeinu Shmuel raised a difficulty: Does the verse not imply that the hammer shatters the rock, since it is not written "and the hammer, the rock will shatter it," and so too we see that a hammer shatters rocks! And one cannot read [the text as] "just as a rock divides into several fragments," for the utterance — that is, the Torah — is likened to a hammer and not to a rock. And in the Commentary [Rashi] he explained: "Just as a hammer" — [meaning] the rock divides through it. But this is not satisfactory, because the utterance itself divides, so it is not a complete analogy. And Rabbeinu Tam says that the verse is speaking of a stone that shatters iron, as it states in Midrash Chazit [Shir HaShirim Rabbah]: An incident occurred with someone who bought a sapphire [sanpirin] and came to test it; he placed it on the anvil and struck it with a sledgehammer — the hammer split and the anvil broke, while the sapphire did not budge from its place, and that is what is written: "And like a hammer that shatters a rock." And even though it is not written "a rock will shatter it," there are many verses like this, [such as] "Waters wear away stones" (Job 14:19) — meaning, the water wore them away. And this fits well with what is stated in the first chapter of Kiddushin (30b): The school of Rabbi Yishmael taught: "My son, if this repulsive one [the evil inclination] encounters you, drag it to the study hall; if it is [like] stone, it dissolves, as it is stated: 'Waters wear away stones'" — meaning, the water wore them away — "and if it is [like] iron, it shatters" — meaning, if the evil inclination grows strong against him like iron, it shatters, as it is stated: "And like a hammer that shatters a rock." And even though there it compares the evil inclination to a hammer whereas here it compares words of Torah to a hammer, there is no concern, for one verse yields several meanings.
